# Benchmark baseline of internal/bid on darwin/arm64 (target T1.6.4).
#
# PROVISIONAL. Taken on a machine shared with other agents' builds and tests:
# load average 23.79 29.36 31.42 at the start of the run, 17.91 23.84 28.55 at
# its end (uptime, 1, 5 and 15 minutes), on a 16-core Apple M4 Max under
# macOS 26. Retake it on a quiet machine, and with a 5% band, before any
# figure here is quoted as the cost of an operation.
#
# Taken on 2026-10-31 at 73a8a451d3 plus the benchmark file, with
#   go test -c -o bid.test internal/bid
#   ./bid.test -test.run XXX -test.bench BenchmarkKernel -test.benchmem \
#       -test.count 8 -test.benchtime 100ms
# in the directory src/internal/bid, and the lines below are that output
# unedited. The file is in benchstat form; compare a later run with
#   benchstat testdata/bench_baseline_darwin_arm64.txt new.txt
#
# Rows are Op/Width/Class. Width 64 and 128 are the decimal kernel; float64 is
# the reference row, where the language has a counterpart. Every row includes
# a loop floor of about 0.9 ns (the float64 add row is nearly all floor).
#
# The ratchet is TestBenchRatchet, opt-in:
#   go test -run TestBenchRatchet internal/bid -args -bid.ratchet
# It measures each row in short runs and takes the smallest time, as it does
# for the samples below. A row fails when its time is over
#   baseline * (1 + ratchet-band) + ratchet-slack-ns
# or when it allocates. The band is 20% until a quiet baseline exists; the
# slack stands for the timer resolution on rows of about a nanosecond. The
# baseline moves only by a deliberate commit that replaces this file.
#
# ratchet-band: 0.20
# ratchet-slack-ns: 0.5
#
# linux/amd64: not recorded here. Its baseline is the file
# testdata/bench_baseline_linux_amd64.txt, to be taken by the CI of that
# platform; the ratchet skips a platform with no file.
#
# The strawman is not a row: its kernel is gone from this tree and its
# figures were declared not meaningful by the audit. They are cited, not
# re-measured. The README of the go-decimal-proposal repository, section
# Performance, gives Add 5.0 ns, Multiply 4.9 ns, Divide 20.5 ns (too few
# digits), Compare 3.3 ns for decimal64 against float64 at 1.7, 1.7, 1.6 and
# 1.6 ns. The width spike in the package documentation (doc.go, "Width
# parameterisation"; 2026-10-30, also under a load average near 40) gives, on
# darwin/arm64, Add64 10.8 ns, Mul64 44.6 ns, Add128 29.4 ns, Mul128 266 ns
# for the strawman and 0.71 ns and 0.91 ns for float64 Add and Mul.
goos: darwin
goarch: arm64
pkg: internal/bid
cpu: Apple M4 Max
